applicability: deep-review final-gate guidance and any orchestration running per-task review gates before a whole-branch gate.

evidence.environment: 10-task branch, 19 commits, per-task review gates plus one final whole-branch review
evidence.source_reference: Issue #73 / #77 field report — Ansible estate tranche-1 run, 2026-08-03; caught only at the whole-branch gate

expected_behavior: A final whole-branch review gate explicitly enumerates any task that changed shared execution configuration such as caching, fact gathering, parallelism, or connection behaviour, and then re-derives which other tasks' verification evidence predates or assumes the previous semantics. Per-task verdicts are not treated as composable when a shared-config task is present in the same branch.
observation: On a multi-task branch, one task enabled a 24-hour on-disk fact cache while another task pruned fact-gathering from playbooks on the basis of a static audit. Each task passed its own review. The second task's live verification ran after the first had landed, so its green check proved the warm-cache world rather than a cold one, and the roles deliberately excluded from the prune were exactly those exposed to stale facts. No per-task gate could see the interaction; only the final whole-branch review did.

scope: Multi-task branches where at least one task edits shared execution configuration. Excludes single-task changes and branches with no shared-config edit.

sensitivity_review.statement: Operator attested that the candidate contains no raw transcripts, secrets, credentials, or executable instructions.
